title: Controller-driven burst mitigation and alert de-escalation playbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: After the capacity regression on 2026-02-18 we observed a repeated cascade of burn-rate pagers triggered by transient autoscaler oscillation and cold-cache latency spikes. This ticket defines an actionable playbook and small technical changes to: 1) reduce noisy burn-rate page storms during short-lived capacity events, 2) allow controllers to apply graceful short-term traffic shaping, and 3) introduce staged alert de-escalation so engineers only get paged for sustained impact. Goals: 1) reduce P0/P1 pager volume from burn-rate rules by 60% for transient events, 2) eliminate duplicate pages for the same underlying root cause, 3) preserve SLO detection sensitivity for real regressions. This effort intentionally focuses on controller-side mitigation (autoscaler backoff, token-budgeting, short-lived circuit breakers) paired with alerting changes (soft-pager for first-minute burn, staggered escalation, aggregated root-cause grouping).
acceptance_criteria: 1) Playbook documented in Confluence with step-by-step triage and runbook links; 2) Controller implements two new knobs: short-lived token-budget (default 30s) and burst hysteresis (configurable); 3) Burn-rate alerts updated to use 3-tier escalation: soft-notify -> on-call-page -> escalation; 4) Pager volume for incident class 'transient-capacity' reduced by >=60% in A/B pilot; 5) New PRs merged and e2e tests added to prevent regressions.
implementation_notes: Proposed technical changes: (A) Controller token-budget: allow the request controller to apply a temporary per-pool token budget that drops non-critical background traffic when the pool is entering burst saturation; (B) Autoscaler smoothing: add a short dampening window after scale events to prevent oscillation-driven capacity tears; (C) Alert policy updates: add a 30s soft-window for new burn-rate signals that emits slack notifications and only pages after sustained 3-minute burn or repeated soft-notifies; (D) Root-cause dedupe: run an aggregation pass in the alert pipeline to group signals by fingerprint (model+region+route) and collapse redundant pages; (E) Lightweight ML classifier: pilot a simple decision tree to suppress low-confidence burn signals likely driven by noise. Trade-offs: token-budgeting risks increasing tail latency for low-priority customers; we'll restrict to non-enterprise tiers and expose opt-out. Handoff: Eng on-call will run the playbook for the next 6 weeks, then we evaluate metrics and expand to Dedicated clusters.

2026-02-24 Diego Ramirez: Spike complete for controller token-budget prototype. Local sims show ~40% fewer dropped requests during synthetic bursts. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/7894
2026-02-27 SRE Review (Lina Zhang): Agreed on soft-pager path but requested conservative defaults (token_budget=20s, hysteresis=15%). Added requirement for per-customer opt-out flags.
2026-03-02 Product (Samir Khan): Confirmed customer tiers: enterprise and compliance customers must be excluded by default. Will add label and gating in console UX work.
2026-03-05 Diego Ramirez: Implemented alert aggregation fingerprint; pushed new alert pipeline config to staging. Grafana dashboard updated: https://grafana.redwood.com/d/alerts/slo-burn
2026-03-08 QA (Marta Silva): Running A/B pilot on 3 clusters. Early data: soft-notify reduced immediate pages by 52% without missing sustained regressions. Recording findings in Confluence.
2026-03-10 Aisha Patel: Requested schedule for rollout to production after one more week of A/B data. Added follow-up sub-issues for console gating and audit logs.
notes: Pilot approach: run token-budgeting behind a feature flag; run A/B across 20% of the fleet for two weeks; collect metrics: pages_per_incident, time_to_detection, false_positive_rate.
Rollout plan: staging -> canary -> global. Post-rollout check-in scheduled for 2026-04-05.
